chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the fasting person vomits, he must make up that day; but if he controls the vomit without actually vomiting, he should complete his fast."
ai.seo_question: Does involuntary vomiting break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on medical treatments for the fasting, this hadith clarifies the distinction between involuntary and voluntary vomiting. It establishes that if one can restrain the vomit from exiting the mouth, the fast remains valid, emphasizing the principle of *istit'ah* (ability) in breaking the fast.
